relationships.subject: joint acidosis
relationships.evidence_quote: Protons act as signals via ASIC1a in chondrocytes, where acidification triggers Ca2+ influx, mitochondrial stress, and apoptosis

relationships.subject: ASIC1a
relationships.evidence_quote: pharmacologic or genetic ASIC1a inhibition reduces acid-induced death

relationships.subject: ASIC3
relationships.evidence_quote: Protons activate joint nociceptors via ASIC3, producing rapid neuronal depolarization and action potential firing; sustained exposure and channel cross-talk (e.g., TRPV1) can further amplify pain signaling

relationships.subject: GPR132
relationships.evidence_quote: G2A activation can sensitize TRPV1 via PKC in sensory neurons, linking acidic/lipidic milieus to pain

relationships.subject: GPR68
relationships.evidence_quote: GPR68 activation can suppress catabolic gene expression (e.g., MMP-13) in inflamed chondrocytes

key_findings: Localized joint acidosis in OA cartilage and meniscus (pH ~6.4-6.7) is masked by near-neutral bulk synovial fluid.
Protons engage ASIC1a, ASIC3, TRPV1 and proton-sensing GPCRs (GPR4/65/68/132) linking acidity to cartilage catabolism and pain.
